relationships.subject: carrageenan
relationships.evidence_quote: Unilateral intramuscular injection of carrageenan, a classical model of inflammatory muscle pain, increased VEGF-A gene expression in the tissues surrounding the injection site.

relationships.subject: VEGF-A165
relationships.evidence_quote: Intramuscular administration of recombinant VEGF-A165 on the same side induced cutaneous mechanical hyperalgesia during the acute and subacute phases.

relationships.subject: VEGFR1
relationships.evidence_quote: The application of a specific VEGFR1 antibody on the same side significantly reduced the mechanical hyperalgesia induced by carrageenan or VEGF-A165 injection

relationships.subject: capsazepine
relationships.evidence_quote: Local preinjection of capsazepine, a transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) antagonist, also inhibited VEGF-A165-induced hyperalgesia.

key_findings: Intramuscular carrageenan-induced cutaneous mechanical hyperalgesia depends on VEGF-A165 acting via VEGFR1 and TRPV1
VEGF-A165-induced hyperalgesia absent in TRPV1 knockout mice in subacute phase
